solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Craft's put in to make thinner book

indicators.note: put in tells us the vessel is placed inside the phrase for diluting

parts.note: to water down a drink is to dilute it, making it thinner
a craft is a vessel such as a ship; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone diluting a manuscript by inserting a boat, or a craft added to slim down a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make thinner' reads like the purpose of the insertion, but it is the phrasal verb being split open; 'book' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Adams's novel about rabbits is named after a hill in Hampshire; a novel is a book.

clue.text: Things wail wildly around heartless group flying up for this?

definitions.text: Things wail wildly around heartless group flying up for this?

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters wrap round the other piece
wildly signals that the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order
in a down clue, flying up means the piece is read from bottom to top
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Wailing creatures and a flying group suggest witches' revels on their night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves GRUP and 'flying up' turns that upwards; 'wildly' scrambles the first two words around it. The whole clue also describes the witches' sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: On the eve of May Day, folklore has witches flying to the Brocken to gather, with things wailing round them.

clue.text: Weaver is the source for this northern river

definitions.text: Weaver is the source for this
definitions.meaning: a rough woollen cloth produced by weavers on looms
the river forming part of the border between Scotland and England

explanation.surface: A weaver supposedly being the origin of a river in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth takes its name, by legend, from the Scottish border river, so one word covers both fabric and waterway.

clue.text: Be sent around to work on Queen on gold coins

parts.note: to run a machine is to work it
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the rand is South Africa's currency, famous through the gold Krugerrand

explanation.surface: Someone sent on their rounds to work on the Queen's gold coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link here, simply placing the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing small jobs for someone means being dispatched to various places on their behalf.

clue.text: Balmoral, say, soundly vetoed one ringing the crown

parts.note: a balmoral is a Scottish flat bonnet, an example of a hat

indicators.note: soundly tells us to take a word as it is heard, not as spelt

parts.note: something vetoed is banned

explanation.surface: The royal Scottish castle firmly forbidden, with a ring round the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is also a royal castle in Scotland, which is what makes 'crown' seem royal; here it is the cap, and the crown is the top of the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon is wrapped round the crown of a hat, encircling it.

clue.text: Regularly appears to unrobe? That leads to trouble

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps appearing to undress causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'appears to unrobe' spell the answer; 'That leads to' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or unsettle someone is to cause them worry and disquiet.

clue.text: Unwilling to cut large obscenity

indicators.note: to cut means the letter for large is to be removed from the word

parts.note: loath means reluctant or unwilling
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to remove a big piece of filth.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word or curse is an obscenity, an old sense of the word for a sworn promise.

clue.text: Head managed emergency room, containing one easy problem

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: containing means the assembled pieces hold the numeral inside them

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
I is the Roman numeral one
ER is the US abbreviation for an emergency room

explanation.surface: A hospital chief running the casualty department with one simple task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' applies to the whole run of three pieces, so the numeral lands in the middle of the second one.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision so obvious that it requires no thought is something simple to solve.

clue.text: Complaint over general fare item

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
the Duke of Wellington was the general who won at Waterloo

explanation.surface: A grievance about the food served by an army general.
explanation.definitionFit: This pastry-wrapped fillet is a dish, a menu item or piece of fare.

clue.text: Prolonged horizontality that is limited by short line

indicators.note: limited by means the abbreviation is bounded on both sides by the other piece
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A long stretch of lying flat, explained by a shortened line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' gives LIN; 'limited by' means that trimmed word encloses the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed past the usual time is a lengthy spell lying down, humorously described.

clue.text: Record support shown by performance chart

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act, as in a music-hall turn
a table is a chart of figures, like a league table

explanation.surface: A record's success shown by a turn on the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record support' looks like backing for a hit single; it is the spinning platter of a deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating platform of a record player holds up the vinyl disc as it plays.

clue.text: Sell short European articles EU gents sent over

parts.note: un is French for a and der is German for the: two European articles

indicators.note: sent over means the following letters are turned round

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a gents toilet

explanation.surface: Bureaucratic items sent to European men by Brussels, undervalued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent over' turns the last two pieces round into VALUE. The articles are one French and one German.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell short is the idiom for failing to give someone or something proper credit, rating it too low.

clue.text: Following craze from the east for flower

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the east means read right to left

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a fad is a passing craze

explanation.surface: A fashion arriving from the East for a particular bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal word for the daffodil, a yellow spring bloom.

clue.text: Some called at Rome on the way back for Italian food

indicators.note: on the way back means the letters are read in reverse order
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Some people called at Rome on their return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'called at Rome' backwards gives E MORTADELLA C.
explanation.definitionFit: This large pork sausage from Bologna is an Italian cold meat.

clue.text: Paid out of capital added to present tax relief

indicators.note: added to means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: a gift is a present

indicators.note: out of capital means the word loses its first letter, its capital

explanation.surface: Paid out of capital to supplement tax relief: a business accounting scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: This UK scheme lets charities reclaim basic-rate income tax on donations, a relief for givers.

clue.text: Large plant flourished a short distance east

parts.note: fl. abbreviates floruit, Latin for flourished, used of a person's active period
a metre is a short distance
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A big plant thriving a little way to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourished' looks like the definition's verb, but it supplies FL.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical tree with scarlet blooms is a large plant.

clue.text: Cake to have covered in cheese

indicators.note: covered in means the verb's synonym is wrapped inside the cheese

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Eating a cake covered in cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small square of rich chocolate cake.

clue.text: Misguided lad sick of northern poets

indicators.note: misguided means the following letters are sent the wrong way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wayward, sick boy among Scandinavian bards.
explanation.definitionFit: Skalds were Old Norse court poets, so the adjective relates to those Scandinavian bards.

clue.text: Monk society cut short raised Cain

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a club is a society

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the name is read upwards

explanation.surface: A monk from a society that was disbanded early raised hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised Cain' is an idiom for making trouble, but here Cain is just turned upside down to NIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A Benedictine of the reformed order based at the abbey of Cluny in Burgundy.

clue.text: Misprint in volume of Alcott heading a line

indicators.note: heading means the first piece goes in front of the rest

parts.note: Louisa May Alcott was American, and in American spelling the unit of volume is liter

explanation.surface: A printing error found in a book by Louisa May Alcott, at the top of a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' seems to be a book; it is the unit of capacity, spelt the American way for an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a typo of a single letter is called by this term.

clue.text: Album playing on journey is a pain

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are set in motion and moved around

parts.note: to go is to journey

explanation.surface: Listening to an album while travelling turns out to be annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower back pain is the ache this word names.

clue.text: American composer is losing pounds

indicators.note: losing means the letter for pounds is dropped from the word

parts.note: to live is to be or exist, so lives can mean is
L stands for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: An American composer is going broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a modernist US composer, also an insurance executive.

clue.text: One surly mongrel gone mad on mire

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
mud is mire

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters have gone crazy, scrambled

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered dog has gone crazy in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges the third word into GEON, which goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered, grumpy person is a surly individual.

clue.text: Last words of unfinished novel I destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and reassembled
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An author destroying an incomplete book, with only the closing lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts NOVEL to NOVE; with I, 'destroyed' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A short concluding stanza of a poem, the closing lines of a work.

clue.text: Cleaner energy protects oxygen

indicators.note: protects means the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: sap is vitality or energy
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A cleaner's energy shielding oxygen: chemistry in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is a washing substance, a cleaning agent.

clue.text: A lot of damage on front of girl's instrument

indicators.note: on front of means the first piece is placed before the second
a lot of means most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: harm is damage
Monica is a girl's name; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Much damage is done to the front of a girl's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth organ is a small reed instrument played by blowing.

clue.text: See vessel that's green

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
a vat is a large vessel

explanation.surface: Look at a container that is coloured green.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a muted grey-green shade used in tweeds.

clue.text: Await speech and coughing

parts.note: to await is to expect
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Waiting for a speech amid a coughing audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Coughing up phlegm or spitting it out is the medical sense here.
